content.text: Confirmed: Array (counterparty) is Delaware/Colorado-based; Ono (our client) is Osaka-based. This matters for the seat analysis.

input.quote: The seat of the arbitration shall be in Osaka, Japan, if it is demanded by Array, and in New York, NY, USA, if it is demanded by Ono, with hearings to held in the same location.
input.rationale: Governing law meets the preferred position exactly: Section 18.3 (p0765) provides that the Agreement "shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York, United States," with CISG excluded. On forum, Section 17.3 (p0747-p0748) provides mandatory ICC arbitration before three arbitrators rather than the preferred New York courts, but this does not reach walk-away territory. Walk-away is defined as the vendor's home jurisdiction with exclusive foreign venue, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad. Here neither seat option is Array's home jurisdiction (Array is a Delaware company based in Boulder, Colorado): the seat is New York, NY when Ono demands arbitration — a fully accepted venue — and Osaka, Japan when Array demands, which is our own client's home city (Ono is organized under the laws of Japan with its principal place of business in Osaka). The demand-based election is reciprocal and, in the only case where the seat falls outside the accepted list, it lands on our home turf, so that limb benefits our party and we do not flag it. Court access is also preserved: each Party retains the right to apply to any court of competent jurisdiction for provisional and conservatory relief (p0757), and either Party may seek recognition and enforcement of any award before any competent court (p0751). Noted in passing but not flagged as deviations: the forum is arbitration rather than courts, the Emergency Arbitrator Provisions are disapplied, and Section 18.3 governing law is carved out from procedural issues (p0749) — sub-elements short of preferred wording that do not disadvantage us given the New York substantive law and preserved court remedies.
